text: what about breaking the uv out into parts, like, split the uv across multiple images and then piece back together. you could normalize every small bit into a fixed size on one atlas and put everything else on the other. this requires more direct prompting influence but is entirely still possible
resolution: Implemented and measured the mutation-free two-zone UV planner on Moped_50. The 477 logical islands reduce to 250 unique paint footprints after 64 additional repeat stacks, a 47.6% reduction. Detail-bearing hero footprints retain natural scale at 1.0; support footprints remain proportional unless undersized, where a 1024-texel-area readability floor raised 41 of 112 footprints while 71 remained natural and none hit the 4x cap. Generated hero and support sheets compile into one 1651x1899 runtime atlas; purple guide substrate was removed and replaced with deterministic ivory/steel bases plus transparent material-detail overlays. Banked reversible paint variant Ivory Two-Zone. Post-layout and post-save semantic status is healthy at 2046/2046 named saved, mounted, and resident faces with 0 unnamed. Coverage save cleared 1,380,625 unsampled pixels with a 2-texel gutter. The legacy 441 x/m UI readout is now explicitly labeled as a target because mixed proportional/floor layouts do not have one actual global density. User visual review remains the acceptance gate.
